Write the root README.md (see files[]) as a thin pointer: one-paragraph monorepo overview + table linking to apps/extension/README.md (the existing extension docs, untouched) and apps/desktop/README.md (the new Tauri app). name: build

# Build the extension package with Docker on pushes to main, pull requests, version
# tags, and manual runs. Scoped to changes under apps/extension/ so unrelated
# desktop-app changes don't rebuild the extension.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
    paths:
      - 'apps/extension/**'
      - '.github/workflows/build.yml'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'apps/extension/**'
      - '.github/workflows/build.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write # required to create a Release on tag builds

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Build with Docker and export the artifact (zip) to apps/extension/dist.
      # The build context is apps/extension (it holds the Dockerfile + .dockerignore);
      # --target export selects the scratch stage; --output writes it to the host.
      - name: Build extension package (Docker)
        run: docker build --target export --output type=local,dest=apps/extension/dist apps/extension

      - name: List artifacts
        run: ls -lh apps/extension/dist

      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: shot2issue-extension
          path: apps/extension/dist/*.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Attach to Release (on tag)
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: apps/extension/dist/*.zip

# shot2issue (monorepo)

shot2issue captures a screenshot, lets you annotate it, and files it as a GitHub,
GitLab, or YouTrack issue with the image embedded inline. This repository hosts two
apps that share the same annotation engine and issue-provider code.

| App | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser extension | [`apps/extension`](apps/extension/README.md) | Chrome Manifest V3 extension (TypeScript, no framework). Capture a tab or paste an image, annotate, and file an issue. Localized docs: [English](apps/extension/README.md) · [简体中文](apps/extension/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](apps/extension/README.ja.md). |
| Desktop app | [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | Cross-platform Tauri 2 desktop app: global hotkey → screen capture → region/window crop → annotate → file an issue. (Work in progress.) |

## Layout

```
.
├── apps/
│   ├── extension/   # Chrome MV3 extension (moved from the old repo root)
│   └── desktop/     # Tauri 2 desktop app
├── .github/workflows/
│   └── build.yml    # Extension build + release (Docker), scoped to apps/extension/**
├── package.json     # npm workspaces + delegating scripts
└── LICENSE
```

## Common tasks

From the repo root:

```sh
npm run build:ext       # compile + copy assets for the extension
npm run test:unit:ext   # extension unit tests
npm run package:ext     # produce the Chrome Web Store zip (apps/extension/dist)
```

Or work directly inside an app (each app keeps its own scripts and lockfile):

```sh
npm ci --prefix apps/extension && npm run build --prefix apps/extension
```

The extension's release flow is unchanged: push a `v*` tag and the
`build` workflow attaches the zip to a GitHub Release.

risks: GitHub Actions workflow files MUST stay at <repo-root>/.github/workflows/ — they are NOT discovered if moved under apps/extension/. The design keeps .github at root; do not move it. If a future maintainer naively `git mv .github apps/extension/`, CI silently stops running.

The `paths:` filter added to push/pull_request means the extension build will NOT run for changes outside apps/extension/ (e.g. desktop-only commits). This is intended, but note: tag pushes (tags: ['v*']) ALSO carry a `paths` filter — GitHub applies path filters to tag pushes too, so a release tag that only touches files outside apps/extension/** would be skipped. Mitigation: the workflow includes '.github/workflows/build.yml' in paths and, more importantly, real releases bump apps/extension/package.json + manifest.json (under apps/extension/**), so the filter matches. If you want belt-and-suspenders, drop the `paths:` filter from the `push: tags:` trigger by splitting triggers, or keep tagging discipline.

Docker build context change: `docker build ... apps/extension` requires the Dockerfile AND .dockerignore to be inside apps/extension (they are, after the move). If the Dockerfile were left at root, `COPY . .` would copy the whole monorepo (including apps/desktop and node_modules) and build.sh would fail. Verify the Dockerfile moved.

If npm workspaces hoist dependencies to a root node_modules, the Dockerfile's `npm ci` inside apps/extension still works because the Dockerfile copies only apps/extension and runs npm ci against apps/extension/package-lock.json in isolation (no root context). But a developer running `npm ci` at the REPO ROOT will install BOTH workspaces and may hoist; that's fine for local dev but means the extension's lockfile and a root lockfile could drift. Recommendation (in steps): keep apps/extension/package-lock.json authoritative and do NOT commit a root package-lock.json, or accept workspace hoisting and update the Dockerfile to copy the repo root — pick one; the design chose the isolated-extension-lockfile path to minimize churn.

Untracked dev dirs at the old root (node_modules/, build/, dist/) are NOT moved by `git mv` (they're gitignored). They will linger at /root/shot2issue/node_modules etc. and could confuse a local `npm` run that picks up the stale root install. Step 5 deletes them; if skipped, an old root node_modules with the old (extension) package.json's deps may mask workspace resolution issues.

The smoke.mjs and screenshots.mjs Playwright tests run headless:false and need xvfb + downloaded browsers — this constraint is pre-existing and unchanged by the move, but the move does not fix it; CI still only runs the Docker build (no tests), matching the original build.yml.

`git mv` preserves history only if committed as a rename without simultaneous content edits. The workflow file edit (build.yml) and the new root package.json/README/.gitignore are content changes to files that did NOT move (build.yml stays at root) or are brand new — so they don't interfere with rename detection of the moved tree. Keep the rename moves and the new-root-file edits reviewable (git status should show R for moved files, A for new root files).

apps/extension/README image paths (src/icons/icon128.png, docs/screenshots/*.png) remain valid ONLY because src/ and docs/ moved together with the README. Confirmed correct in this design — but any future split of README from its assets re-breaks them.

The release.yml 3-platform Tauri matrix + typecheck.yml + scripts/check.sh Docker validation are curvault's shipping CI and are reused VERBATIM by the desktop subsystem (out of scope here, but the monorepo .github layout is designed to host them alongside build.yml).

[package]
name = "shot2issue"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "shot2issue — global-hotkey screen capture that files annotated screenshots as issues."
authors = ["wa-otomia"]
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.77"

[lib]
name = "shot2issue_lib"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["macos-private-api", "tray-icon", "image-png"] }
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
tauri-plugin-shell = "2"
tauri-plugin-store = "2"
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"
tauri-plugin-process = "2"
tauri-plugin-http = "2"
tauri-plugin-global-shortcut = "2"

serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
thiserror = "1"
anyhow = "1"

# Screen capture: multi-monitor grab + per-window enumeration on
# Win / macOS / X11. Wayland falls back to the XDG Desktop Portal (see
# services/capture.rs) since xcap cannot grab there.
xcap = "0.0.14"
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["png"] }
base64 = "0.22"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
# Query the active Screen Recording (TCC) authorization so the UI can guide
# the one-time grant + restart instead of capturing a black frame.
core-graphics = "0.24"

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
lto = true
opt-level = "s"
panic = "abort"
strip = true

designs.summary: Design for the capture-hotkey-overlay subsystem of the new apps/desktop Tauri 2 app. It registers a user-rebindable global shortcut (tauri-plugin-global-shortcut) that fires while the app is backgrounded; on fire the Rust backend detects which monitor the OS cursor is on (xcap Monitor::from_point), captures that full monitor to PNG bytes, and stashes the frozen frame in shared state. The frontend then runs one of two crop UXs: (A) region-crop via a transparent, fullscreen, always-on-top, skip-taskbar overlay WebviewWindow that paints the frozen screenshot and lets the user rubber-band a rectangle (Win/macOS/X11); (B) window-pick, listing top-level windows via xcap with their bounds so the user clicks one and we crop the frozen frame to that window's rect. On native Wayland (detected at runtime) the live overlay is impossible, so we degrade: capture full monitor, then open a normal in-app window where the same crop UI runs against the static image (no always-on-top, no positioning). The cropped PNG is handed to the reused shot2issue canvas editor by staging it exactly as the extension's stageAndOpen did — a data-URL attachment in a pending-shots store — and routed to an `editor` window label. All capture/window/crop work happens in Rust and crosses IPC as base64 PNG + integer rects; no webview fetch/canvas-of-the-desktop is used, which keeps it WKWebView/CORS-safe. Everything here is NEW code (xcap, global-shortcut are not in curvault); the window-creation, command-registration, api.ts wrapper, capabilities-per-label, and event plumbing are reused verbatim from curvault's proven patterns.

files.purpose: Core capture service (NEW). Detects the monitor under the cursor, captures a full-monitor PNG, lists top-level windows with bounds, and crops a previously frozen frame to a rect or to a window. Holds the most-recent frozen frame in process state so the overlay can re-request bytes and the crop step can run server-side (no desktop pixels ever touch the webview). Returns base64 PNG over IPC. <=400 lines.

Global-shortcut registration + cursor read + the capture->overlay orchestration (NEW). Registers a rebindable accelerator via tauri-plugin-global-shortcut, reads the true OS cursor on fire, calls capture::capture_at, then asks the overlay module to spawn/position the overlay (or the degraded normal window on Wayland). Holds the active accelerator so a rebind can unregister the old one.

Overlay window lifecycle (NEW). Creates the transparent fullscreen always-on-top skip-taskbar overlay over the captured monitor (Win/macOS/X11); on native Wayland creates a normal in-app crop window instead. Stores the latest MonitorShot so the overlay webview can pull it on load. Implements click-through toggling via set_ignore_cursor_events for the dimmed non-selection region.

Tauri command surface for capture (NEW; same shape as curvault's commands.rs — thin wrappers delegating to services, returning services::Result). These are the #[tauri::command] signatures the prompt asked for.

Front-end capture-flow module (NEW). The TS counterpart to curvault's src/lib/api.ts: thin invoke() wrappers for every capture command + event listeners, PLUS the orchestration that ties hotkey-fired capture -> overlay UI -> crop/window-pick -> hand PNG to the editor. Components never import @tauri-apps/api directly.

The overlay window's React UI (NEW), rendered when main.tsx sees window label === 'overlay'. Paints the frozen MonitorShot full-bleed, implements rubber-band region select (with dimmed mask + live dimensions readout), a mode toggle to window-pick (highlights window bounds from listWindows on hover, click to confirm), and Enter/Esc handling. Detailed skeleton; full impl is straightforward DOM math.

Window-label dispatch (NEW; copies curvault's main.tsx pattern of reading __TAURI_INTERNALS__ metadata.currentWindow.label). Routes the 'overlay' label to Overlay, 'editor' to the reused shot2issue editor view, else the main app shell.

Overlay styling (NEW), in the curvault design language (cyan accent #36c5ff, navy dim). Full-bleed frozen frame, a dim mask, a bright cyan selection border with a punch-through (clear) interior via box-shadow spread, a size badge, and a centered hint pill.

Capabilities for the overlay window-label (NEW; copies curvault's per-label capability file pattern). Grants only what the overlay needs: window control, the capture/overlay commands (via core invoke), and event listening.

Implement services/overlay.rs: is_wayland() runtime detection; present() branches to present_overlay (transparent + always_on_top + skip_taskbar + position/inner_size over the captured monitor) or present_windowed (normal centered decorated window) on Wayland. Stash the MonitorShot in a static so the overlay webview pulls it via get_overlay_shot. Add set_click_through (set_ignore_cursor_events) and dismiss.

Wire commands.rs with the #[tauri::command] signatures (get_default_accelerator, set_capture_hotkey, trigger_capture, capture_current_monitor, get_overlay_shot, list_windows, capture_window, crop_region, overlay_set_click_through, overlay_dismiss, open_editor_with) and register them all in lib.rs invoke_handler; add the global-shortcut + http plugins and the setup-time hotkey registration.

Add src-tauri/capabilities/overlay.json granting the overlay window-label only window-control + event-listen + core invoke; mirror curvault's default.json for the main window and editor.json for the editor window.

Build the front-end: src/lib/capture.ts (invoke wrappers + confirmRegion/confirmWindow/cancelCapture orchestration), src/views/Overlay.tsx (frozen-frame paint, rubber-band region select with dim/punch-through, Tab-toggle window-pick with hover-highlight + click-confirm, Enter/Esc), src/overlay.css (curvault palette). Route via main.tsx window-label dispatch.

Port the shot2issue canvas editor into src/views/Editor.tsx: keep editor.ts's canvas engine verbatim, but replace the chrome.storage pendingShots staging with a Rust-side editor_stage service (open_editor_with stashes the PNG; the editor window reads it on mount via a get_pending_shots command) so the data-URL-attachment contract from the extension's stageAndOpen is preserved 1:1.

Add a system tray (tray-icon feature) with a 'Capture now' item calling trigger_capture and a 'Capture shortcut…' submenu — this is the mandatory fallback trigger on native Wayland where the global hotkey can't register.
Verify the X11/Win/mac paths on real hardware (see validationNotes); on Linux the implementer can only smoke-test the Wayland-degrade window path and the xcap X11 path under an X session.
risks: xcap API surface drift: method names (Monitor::from_point, scale_factor(), Window::id()/title()/app_name()/is_minimized(), capture_image()) and whether they return Result vs plain values differ across xcap 0.0.x releases. Pin an exact version and adjust the .map_err/?? as the chosen version dictates — the version in Cargo.toml (0.0.14) is illustrative and MUST be checked against docs.rs at implementation time.

Coordinate-space mismatch is the single biggest correctness risk. xcap reports monitor/window geometry and captures in DEVICE pixels; the overlay window is sized in LOGICAL px; tauri's cursor_position is global but its logical/physical-ness varies by platform. The design funnels everything through one scale factor per monitor and reports logical px to the front end, but the exact logical/physical of cursor_position and window bounds must be verified per-OS (especially mixed-DPI multi-monitor on Windows and Retina+external on macOS).

tauri-plugin-global-shortcut chord syntax: 'Cmd+Shift+4' vs 'CommandOrControl+Shift+4' vs 'Super'. The Shortcut::from_str grammar must be matched exactly or register() Errs at runtime; also some chords (Cmd+Shift+3/4/5 on macOS) collide with the OS screenshot service and silently lose to the system — pick a default that doesn't collide, or document the collision.

macOS Screen Recording (TCC): xcap capture returns black/blank frames until the user grants Screen Recording in System Settings AND restarts the app. The first capture must detect an all-black/empty frame and route the user to the TCC grant flow. Self-signed (not notarized) signing in CI is what keeps that grant stable across updates — if the signing identity changes, the grant is revoked and capture silently breaks.

Overlay transparency + always-on-top reliability: on macOS, transparent(true) requires macOSPrivateApi (set) and still occasionally needs set_fullscreen(false)+exact size to avoid Space animations; on some Linux X11 WMs always_on_top from the builder is ignored (we re-assert via set_always_on_top). Multi-monitor with a menu bar/taskbar on the captured monitor may leave a strip uncovered — verify the overlay truly covers the whole display.

Memory: a 4K/5K monitor frame is ~30-60 MB of RGBA held in the LAST_FRAME Mutex plus a multi-MB base64 PNG crossing IPC. Acceptable for a transient capture, but the frame must be cleared on overlay dismiss to avoid retaining it for the whole session.

set_ignore_cursor_events for window-pick click-through is platform-inconsistent (and a no-op on Wayland). The window-pick mode as designed reads window bounds and confirms inside the overlay without needing true click-through, which sidesteps this — but if a future design wants the cursor to fall through to the real window under it, that path needs per-OS verification.
validationNotes: PROVEN by curvault, reuse verbatim: the Tauri builder/plugin wiring, services-layer error type + Result + OnceLock app-handle injection, WebviewWindowBuilder for transparent/frameless/decorations(false)/transparent(true)/center() windows (curvault's open_popup does exactly this and ships), per-window-label capability JSON files, window-label dispatch in main.tsx via __TAURI_INTERNALS__, the src/lib/api.ts invoke-wrapper convention, the updater (minisign pubkey + GitHub latest.json) and the release.yml tauri-action matrix, the macOSPrivateApi + windowEffects config, and the reqwest-in-Rust networking pattern. The design copies these one-to-one.

NEW and unproven (not present in curvault), MUST be verified on real machines: everything touching xcap (monitor-under-cursor detection, full-monitor and per-window capture, scale-factor handling), tauri-plugin-global-shortcut registration + the actual chord firing while backgrounded, the live transparent always-on-top overlay positioned exactly over one monitor, set_ignore_cursor_events behavior, and the cursor_position coordinate space. None of these can be exercised on the implementer's Linux/Wayland host.

VERIFIABLE on the implementer's Linux box (partial): under an X11 session, xcap capture + global-shortcut + the transparent overlay can be smoke-tested. The Wayland-degrade path (normal centered window, no always-on-top) can be tested directly under Wayland. So Linux/X11 + Linux/Wayland-degrade are reachable locally; macOS (TCC grant, transparent window, Carbon hotkey, self-signed-signing grant stability) and Windows (mixed-DPI geometry, mica overlay, NSIS signing placeholder) require CI artifacts run on real mac/win hardware or a tester.

The editor contract is verified by inspection of shot2issue: the canvas editor consumes attachments whose only required field for rendering is a `dataUrl` PNG string (editor.ts loadActive sets baseImage.src = a.dataUrl). The desktop app therefore only needs to produce a PNG data URL and stage it the same way background.ts's stageAndOpen does — this is a faithful reuse, not a rewrite, and needs only that the staging store be swapped from chrome.storage to a Rust command (get/set pending shot).

macOS self-signed signing keeping the TCC Screen-Recording grant stable across updates is an ASSUMPTION carried from the prior research brief; it is NOT exercised by curvault (which has no screen capture and no TCC dependency). It must be validated end-to-end on a real Mac: grant once, ship an update signed with the SAME self-signed identity, confirm capture still returns real (non-black) pixels without re-prompting.

designs.summary:
Design for the editor-reuse-upload subsystem of the new Tauri desktop app (apps/desktop/), reusing shot2issue's annotation editor + issue-upload + AI by extracting a framework-agnostic core into packages/core/ and injecting platform adapters.

CORE INSIGHT: shot2issue's editor.ts (2016 lines) is NOT reusable as-is — it is a load-time IIFE bound to fixed DOM ids, chrome.storage, chrome.tabs, chrome.runtime, navigator.mediaDevices/clipboard. But the *annotation engine inside it* (drawOne/drawArrow/drawPen/drawMosaic/drawNumRect/wrapText/renderOps, the bbox/handle/hit-test geometry, the crop math, offsetOp/opIntersects) is PURE: it touches only a CanvasRenderingContext2D, an HTMLImageElement, and Op[]. That pure engine is what ports verbatim; the DOM glue, event wiring, storage, tabs, and the streaming-bubble UI get rewritten as a React component that calls the engine.

Three reuse tiers:
- REUSE VERBATIM (move to packages/core, zero edits): lib/types.ts, lib/providers/types.ts, lib/providers/index.ts, the pure halves of lib/ai.ts (PKCE, JWT, quota/model/title/complaint parsing, request builders, streamResponse) and lib/i18n.ts (t/setLanguage/localizeDom/detectLang — detectLang already falls back to navigator). The canvas-engine functions extracted out of editor.ts into core/canvas/engine.ts.
- ADAPT (same logic, swap 2-3 calls): lib/gitlab.ts, lib/youtrack.ts and their provider wrappers — replace window.fetch with an injected HttpFetch (Rust reqwest via tauri-plugin-http) so CORS works on WKWebView, and replace chrome.permissions.* with a no-op (Tauri has no per-origin permission prompt). ai.ts flows (generateTitle/generateComplaint/transcribeAudio/refresh) take the same HttpFetch + a StoragePort instead of chrome.storage. storage.ts is rewritten over tauri-plugin-store but keeps the exact same function signatures.
- REWRITE (chrome mechanism has no Tauri equivalent): the GitHub provider. github-attach.ts + page-upload.ts depend on chrome.scripting.executeScript injecting into github.com's own React composer to get a same-origin attachment upload with NO token — there is no Tauri analogue. The desktop GitHub provider becomes a PAT + REST/GraphQL client (upload image bytes to a repo/gist via the Contents API, embed the raw URL, then create the issue), structurally identical to the gitlab.ts client. Also rewritten: the Codex OAuth loopback — replace the chrome.tabs.onUpdated ?code= capture with a ~30-line Rust 127.0.0.1:1455 /auth/callback server.

The React editor wrapper (AnnotationCanvas.tsx + useAnnotator hook) owns the canvas element and all pointer/keyboard state that editor.ts kept in module globals, and delegates every pixel to the verbatim engine. Issue upload runs entirely in TS calling httpFetch (Rust does the socket I/O); only OAuth-loopback and the raw HTTP transport live in Rust.

files.purpose: New workspace package holding the framework-agnostic, platform-free core shared by apps/extension and apps/desktop. No chrome.*, no @tauri-apps, no DOM-id assumptions. Pure TS compiled with tsc; consumed as source by both apps' bundlers.

THE adapter contract. Every platform-coupled capability the reused code needs becomes a port interface here. apps/extension supplies chrome-backed impls; apps/desktop supplies tauri-backed impls. This is the single seam that lets the verbatim code run in either host.

The annotation engine extracted VERBATIM from shot2issue/src/editor.ts. Pure rendering + geometry: no DOM ids, no events, no storage. Operates only on a CanvasRenderingContext2D, a CanvasImageSource, and Op[]. This is the single biggest piece of reuse — ~450 lines lifted with zero behavioral change (function bodies copied exactly), only made into named exports.

Rewrite of shot2issue/src/lib/storage.ts over a StoragePort instead of chrome.storage.local directly. KEEPS EVERY EXPORTED SIGNATURE (getConfig/patchConfig/getPendingShots/setPendingShots/getEditorPrefs/patchEditorPrefs/getAiAuth/setAiAuth/patchAiAuth/getPendingAuth/...), so editor logic and ai.ts call sites are unchanged. All default-config + migrateAccounts logic copied verbatim (it is pure).

A module-level injected HttpFetch + a shim that lets the verbatim-ported ai.ts / gitlab.ts / youtrack.ts keep calling a `fetch`-shaped function. This is the seam that routes all network IO through Rust reqwest on desktop (CORS-safe on WKWebView) while the extension binds it to window.fetch.

shot2issue/src/lib/ai.ts ADAPTED: all pure helpers (PKCE, JWT, parseQuotaHeaders, buildTitlePrompt, buildResponsesRequest, cleanTitle, extractOutputText, streamResponse, parseModelsResponse, parseComplaintOutput, partialComplaintFields, buildComplaintRequest) are VERBATIM. Only: (1) `import { fetch } from '../net'` replaces the global, (2) getAiAuth/setAiAuth come from ../storage (already port-backed), (3) the chrome-only flows (ensureAiPermissions, connectViaCallbackCapture) are removed; connect() uses the OAuthLoopbackPort. nowMs() uses the injected Platform.now.

REWRITTEN GitHub provider. The extension's github.com same-origin composer injection (chrome.scripting.executeScript) has NO Tauri equivalent, so desktop uses a Personal Access Token + the REST/GraphQL API. Structurally mirrors gitlab.ts: upload each image's bytes to an attachments path, embed the URL, then create the issue. This is the only provider that is a true rewrite rather than an adapt.

The DESKTOP implementation of the core's Platform ports, wired once at app boot. This is where @tauri-apps actually appears. Binds the core's net/storage/now seams, then everything in packages/core runs unchanged.

Curvault-convention invoke() chokepoint for the desktop app's own (non-core) Tauri commands: hotkey, screen capture, window pick, OAuth loopback. The frontend never imports @tauri-apps/api directly outside platform.ts + this file (CLAUDE.md rule).

The React wrapper that REPLACES editor.ts's DOM glue. It owns the <canvas>, holds the pointer/selection/crop/text state that editor.ts kept in module globals, and delegates every draw/hit-test to packages/core/canvas/engine (verbatim engine). This + useAnnotator is the bulk of the new editor code; the rendering math itself is reused, not rewritten.

Hook that ports editor.ts's interaction logic (mousedown/mousemove/mouseup/keydown handlers, redraw loop, openTextBox/commitTextIfAny, crop drag, selection drag/resize) into React refs. The PURE math (bbox/handle/resize/crop/render) is delegated to the engine; only the stateful event wiring is rewritten. Kept under 400 lines per CLAUDE.md by leaning on the engine.

The full editor page composing the canvas wrapper + toolbar + form + AI controls, styled with curvault tokens. Replaces editor.html + the form/AI half of editor.ts. Drives submit() through the verbatim provider registry (getProvider) and the AI streaming through core ai.ts; capture/voice use the desktop ports.

The Codex OAuth loopback server — the clean Rust replacement for the extension's chrome.tabs.onUpdated ?code= capture. ~30 lines: bind 127.0.0.1:1455, read the GET line of the first request to /auth/callback, return its full URL to the awaiting command, serve a small 'you may close this tab' HTML page.

Core barrel + the one initCore() call the host makes at boot to inject the Platform (binds net, storage, now). After this, every reused module (ai.ts, gitlab.ts, youtrack.ts, storage.ts, providers) runs with no further wiring.

steps: Scaffold the monorepo: create packages/core/ and apps/desktop/, move the existing extension to apps/extension/ (update scripts/build.sh, Dockerfile, .github/workflows/build.yml, tests/*.mjs paths — keep them green). Add a root package.json with npm workspaces (packages/core, apps/extension, apps/desktop).
Create packages/core/src/ports.ts and net.ts (the HttpFetch + StoragePort + OAuthLoopbackPort + ShellPort contracts and the injected `fetch`/`bindHttp` seam).
Move VERBATIM into packages/core/src: types.ts, i18n.ts, providers/types.ts, providers/index.ts. These compile unchanged (i18n.detectLang already has a navigator fallback).

Extract the canvas engine: copy drawOne/drawArrow/drawPen/drawMosaic/drawNumRect/strokeRectHalo/haloWidth/outlineWidth/wrapText/renderOps + bboxOf/boxHandles/handlesOf/handleAt/distToSeg/pointInOp/pointInRect/moveOpBy/resizeOp/normalize + offsetOp/opIntersects + renderAttachmentToDataUrl/downscaleDataUrl out of editor.ts into packages/core/src/canvas/engine.ts as named exports. Change bboxOf/handlesOf/handleAt/pointInOp to take an explicit ctx (for text measurement) and a scale arg (instead of reading the module-global canvas).
Rewrite storage.ts over StoragePort keeping every signature; copy DEFAULT_CONFIG + migrateAccounts + accountFor + id generators verbatim. Add bindStorage.

Adapt ai.ts: copy all pure helpers verbatim; replace global fetch with `import { fetch } from '../net'`; route getAiAuth/setAiAuth through the new storage; delete ensureAiPermissions + connectViaCallbackCapture; add connect(oauth, shell) using the loopback port; add bindNow.

Adapt gitlab.ts + youtrack.ts: swap window.fetch → injected fetch; replace ensureHostPermission (chrome.permissions) with a return-true no-op (Tauri reqwest has no per-origin gate). Keep dataUrlToBlob (FormData multipart still works through tauri-plugin-http). Their provider wrappers (providers/gitlab.ts, providers/youtrack.ts) port verbatim minus the ensureHostPermission import.

Rewrite providers/github.ts as a PAT-based REST/GraphQL client (make GitHub account-based; upload image bytes via repo Contents API or gist, embed the URL, POST /issues). Drop github-attach.ts and page-upload.ts from the desktop build entirely.

Write the Rust side in apps/desktop/src-tauri: oauth_loopback.rs (127.0.0.1:1455 /auth/callback), register Loopback state + oauth_loopback_start/wait commands in lib.rs; add tauri-plugin-http to Cargo.toml and capabilities (http:default scoped to the API hosts), tauri-plugin-store, tauri-plugin-shell.
Write apps/desktop/src/lib/platform.ts (makePlatform) and apps/desktop/src/lib/api.ts; call initCore(await makePlatform()) + setLanguage(config.lang) in main.tsx before rendering EditorView.

Build the React editor: useAnnotator.ts (port the editor.ts pointer/keyboard handlers into refs, delegating math to the engine), AnnotationCanvas.tsx, EditorView.tsx (toolbar + form + AI streaming bubble + submit), styled with curvault index.css tokens copied into apps/desktop/src/index.css.

Port the editor's clipboard-paste-as-attachment and the voice-complaint MediaRecorder flow into EditorView (navigator.mediaDevices/clipboard exist in WKWebView/WebView2; transcribeAudio's FormData goes through tauri-plugin-http). Wire the AI connect button to core ai.connect(platform.oauth, platform.shell).

Add a core unit-test target (tsc + node) reusing the extension's ai-unit/youtrack-unit assertions against packages/core (the pure helpers moved, so the existing tests largely transplant), proving the verbatim extraction didn't drift.
risks: GitHub is a genuine rewrite, not a port. The extension never uses a token — it injects into github.com's own composer for a same-origin upload (page-upload.ts), which is impossible in Tauri. The PAT path has no first-class issue-attachment API: Contents-API/gist uploads work but private-repo raw image URLs require auth to render, so images may 404 for other viewers. Must validate which upload target (repo branch vs public gist vs releases asset) renders inline for the user's repo visibility. This is the highest-uncertainty piece.

tauri-plugin-http's Response must satisfy the core's streamResponse (res.body.getReader()). tauri-plugin-http returns a spec-compliant Response with a readable body, but SSE streaming through Rust reqwest must be confirmed to deliver incremental chunks (not buffered) so the live title/thinking stream still works. If it buffers, the streaming UX silently degrades to a single late update — verify on a real build.

The Codex OAuth client only registers http://localhost:1455 (the extension comment notes chromiumapp.org is rejected). The design uses 127.0.0.1:1455 in the loopback; confirm the registered redirect is host-exact — if it requires the literal string 'localhost' (not 127.0.0.1) the Rust server must bind/advertise 'localhost' and exchangeCode must send the identical redirect_uri.

editor.ts keeps ALL interaction state in module-level `let`s and relies on synchronous redraw after every mutation. Porting to React refs (not useState) preserves the synchronous-redraw model, but any accidental use of state-batching for drawing will introduce lag/flicker. useAnnotator must use refs + manual redraw, never setState-per-pointermove.

navigator.clipboard.write(ClipboardItem) and getUserMedia behave differently across WKWebView (macOS) and WebView2 (Windows). The copy-to-clipboard and voice-dictation paths are reused verbatim but are exactly the APIs most likely to need per-platform fallbacks; cannot be verified on Linux.

The MediaRecorder mimeType (audio/webm) used by the voice flow may not be produced by WKWebView (which historically prefers mp4/aac). transcribeAudio sends whatever blob type it gets; the whisper endpoint may reject an unexpected container. Verify on macOS.

FormData multipart upload (gitlab/youtrack attachments) through tauri-plugin-http: the plugin must forward the multipart boundary correctly. The extension relied on the browser setting the boundary; through Rust reqwest the body must be passed in a way that preserves Content-Type with boundary. Confirm an actual attachment upload succeeds end-to-end.
validationNotes: PROVEN by curvault, reuse verbatim: tauri-plugin-http/store/shell/updater/process wiring, the invoke() chokepoint pattern (api.ts), the transparent-window + windowEffects + macOSPrivateApi config, the GitHub-releases updater (updates.rs + UpdaterWindow.tsx), the curvault design tokens (index.css), the multi-window-by-label bundle pattern (main.tsx currentLabel) — all shipping in curvault 0.1.34.

PROVEN by shot2issue, reuse verbatim (pure, no platform coupling): the entire canvas annotation engine (drawing + geometry + crop + export), all ai.ts parsing/PKCE/prompt/stream helpers, i18n (t/setLanguage/localizeDom), types, the provider interface + registry, the gitlab/youtrack REST clients' logic (only fetch/permission calls swapped). These are already unit-tested in the extension (tests/ai-unit.mjs, youtrack-unit.mjs) and that coverage transplants to packages/core.

MUST VERIFY on a real mac/windows machine — cannot be checked on Linux: (1) SSE streaming actually arrives incrementally through tauri-plugin-http; (2) the Codex localhost:1455 redirect is accepted with the Rust loopback (exact host string); (3) navigator.clipboard.write + getUserMedia + MediaRecorder container work in WKWebView and WebView2; (4) FormData multipart attachment upload preserves the boundary through Rust reqwest; (5) the GitHub PAT image-upload target renders inline for both public and private repos; (6) macOS Screen Recording (TCC) grant survives the self-signed-signing update channel.

CANNOT be validated anywhere in this design pass (out of subsystem scope, flagged for the capture subsystem): the global hotkey, xcap/portal screen capture, and window quick-pick. This subsystem assumes capture hands EditorView a {dataUrl,width,height} via apps/desktop/src/lib/api.ts and is otherwise capture-agnostic.

The 400-line file limit (CLAUDE.md) is at risk only for useAnnotator.ts (editor.ts's interaction half is ~600 lines). Mitigation is real: the pure math moved to the engine, so the hook holds only event wiring + refs; if it still exceeds 400, split crop handling into useCropTool.ts.

designs.summary:
Design for the apps/desktop/ CI signed-build + auto-update subsystem, modeled directly on curvault's shipping setup but adapted for (a) a monorepo working dir (apps/desktop/), (b) a separate desktop-v* tag trigger that coexists with the extension's existing v* build.yml, (c) macOS self-signed code signing in CI from a .p12 secret (NO Apple notarization) to keep the Screen Recording/TCC grant stable across updates, and (d) Windows/Linux OS-signing placeholders that no-op when no cert secret is present. Update delivery is curvault-verbatim: tauri-plugin-updater + minisign TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY + GitHub-released latest.json (includeUpdaterJson). Everything in the "proven by curvault" column is copied as-is; only the macOS .p12 signing, the monorepo projectPath, and the TCC-stability rationale are NEW and must be verified on a real Mac.

Reused verbatim from curvault (proven shipping): tauri-action@v0 3-platform matrix (macos-latest universal / ubuntu-22.04 / windows-latest), TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY + _PASSWORD minisign env, includeUpdaterJson:true, releaseDraft:true, the tauri.conf.json plugins.updater block (active/dialog:false/pubkey/endpoints) and bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts:true, the ubuntu libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev deps line, swatinem/rust-cache, dtolnay/rust-toolchain with mac dual targets.

NEW (must verify on real mac/win): the macOS keychain import + post-build re-codesign step from APPLE_CERTIFICATE/APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD; using tauri-action's built-in APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY env so tauri signs during bundling (preferred over a manual post-step); the self-signed cert's stable hash anchoring the TCC grant; Windows signtool / Linux placeholder steps; projectPath: apps/desktop for the monorepo.

files.path: apps/desktop/.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml — NOTE: GitHub only runs workflows from the repo-root .github/workflows/, so this file actually lives at <repo-root>/.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml. Shown here logically as the desktop app's release flow; place it at repo root alongside the extension's build.yml.
files.purpose: Signed 3-platform Tauri build + GitHub draft release with updater latest.json, triggered ONLY by desktop-v* tags so it coexists with the extension's v* build.yml. Includes macOS self-signed code signing (no notarization), Windows/Linux signing placeholders that skip when secrets absent.
files.content:
name: desktop-release

# Build, sign, and release the desktop (Tauri) app.
# Triggered by desktop-version tags ONLY (desktop-v1.2.3) so this flow is fully
# independent of the extension's `v*` tags handled by .github/workflows/build.yml.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'desktop-v*'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Avoid two release runs for the same tag racing each other.
concurrency:
  group: desktop-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    permissions:
      contents: write # create the GitHub Release + upload assets
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: 'macos-latest'
            args: '--target universal-apple-darwin'
          - platform: 'ubuntu-22.04'
            args: ''
          - platform: 'windows-latest'
            args: ''

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.platform == 'macos-latest' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}

      - name: Cache Cargo
        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/desktop/src-tauri

      - name: Install Linux build deps
        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf \
            libxdo-dev libxcb1-dev libxrandr-dev libdbus-1-dev
          # libxdo / xcb / xrandr: global-shortcut + xcap screen capture on X11.

      # ---- macOS self-signed code signing -------------------------------
      # Import a self-signed cert (.p12) into a throwaway keychain so the .app
      # carries a STABLE code-signing identity. macOS anchors the Screen
      # Recording (TCC) grant to the signature; a stable identity keeps the
      # grant across auto-updates. We do NOT notarize. tauri-action picks up
      # APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY automatically and signs during bundling.
      # The whole block no-ops when APPLE_CERTIFICATE is not set (forks/PRs).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: macos_cert
        if: matrix.platform == 'macos-latest' && env.APPLE_CERTIFICATE != ''
        env:
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          KEYCHAIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/build.keychain-db"
          KEYCHAIN_PW="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PW" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PW" "$KEYCHAIN"
          CERT_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/cert.p12"
          echo "$APPLE_CERTIFICATE" | base64 --decode > "$CERT_PATH"
          security import "$CERT_PATH" -k "$KEYCHAIN" \
            -P "$APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD" \
            -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/security
          # Allow codesign to use the key without an interactive prompt.
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: \
            -s -k "$KEYCHAIN_PW" "$KEYCHAIN" >/dev/null
          # Put our keychain first in the search list so codesign finds it.
          security list-keychains -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN" $(security list-keychains -d user | tr -d '"')
          echo "signing_identity=$APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Imported identities:"
          security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KEYCHAIN"

      - name: Install npm deps
        run: npm ci --prefix apps/desktop

      # ---- Build + sign + release --------------------------------------
      - name: Build and release
        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # minisign updater signing (required — same as curvault):
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # macOS code signing (self-signed, no notarization). Empty on other
          # platforms / when the secret is absent — tauri then skips signing.
          APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ steps.macos_cert.outputs.signing_identity }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          includeUpdaterJson: true
          tagName: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'Shotcap ${{ github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: |
            See the assets attached below for installers.

            - `.dmg` — macOS (universal: Apple Silicon + Intel, self-signed)
            - `.AppImage` / `.deb` — Linux (x86_64)
            - `.exe` (NSIS) / `.msi` — Windows (x86_64)
          releaseDraft: true
          prerelease: false
          args: ${{ matrix.args }}

      # ---- Windows OS signing placeholder ------------------------------
      # No-op unless WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE is provided. When present, sign the
      # produced installers with signtool. (Authenticode is independent of the
      # minisign updater signature, which is already applied above.)
      - name: Sign Windows installers (placeholder)
        if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest' && env.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE != ''
        env:
          WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE }}
          WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $pfx = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\win-cert.pfx"
          [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($pfx, [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE))
          $bundle = "apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle"
          Get-ChildItem -Path $bundle -Recurse -Include *.exe,*.msi | ForEach-Object {
            signtool sign /fd SHA256 /tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
              /f $pfx /p $env:WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD $_.FullName
          }
          # NOTE: signing AFTER tauri-action means re-upload would be needed to
          # attach signed binaries. For production, prefer Tauri's built-in
          # windows.signCommand in tauri.conf.json so signing happens before
          # latest.json is generated. This placeholder documents the hook.

      # ---- Linux OS signing placeholder --------------------------------
      # No-op unless LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY is provided. AppImage/deb signing is
      # optional; the minisign updater signature already covers update trust.
      - name: Sign Linux packages (placeholder)
        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04' && env.LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY != ''
        env:
          LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: |
          echo "$LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" | gpg --batch --import
          BUNDLE=apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle
          find "$BUNDLE" -name '*.AppImage' -o -name '*.deb' | while read -r f; do
            gpg --batch --yes --pinentry-mode loopback \
              --passphrase "$LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE" \
              --detach-sign --armor "$f"
          done
          # Placeholder: detached .asc signatures are produced but not auto-
          # attached to the release. Wire up upload here when a key exists.

files.content:
# Signing & Auto-Update — Shotcap (desktop)

Two *independent* signatures are involved. Don't conflate them:

| Signature | Purpose | Required? | Tooling |
|-----------|---------|-----------|---------|
| **minisign updater signature** | Proves an update artifact is authentic before the app installs it. Verified against the `pubkey` baked into `tauri.conf.json`. | **Yes** | `tauri signer` |
| **macOS code signature (self-signed)** | Gives the `.app` a *stable* code identity so macOS keeps the Screen Recording (TCC) grant across updates. NOT notarization. | Recommended for mac | `security` / `codesign` |
| Windows Authenticode / Linux GPG | OS-level installer trust (SmartScreen / repo signing). | Optional | `signtool` / `gpg` |

The release flow lives in `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` and fires on
`desktop-v*` tags only — completely separate from the extension's `v*`
`build.yml`. Both can release from the same repo without colliding.

---

## 1. Minisign updater keypair (REQUIRED)

Generate once on a trusted machine:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/desktop run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/shotcap.key
# → prompts for a password; writes:
#   ~/.tauri/shotcap.key      (PRIVATE — never commit)
#   ~/.tauri/shotcap.key.pub  (PUBLIC  — paste into tauri.conf.json)
```

- Copy the **contents** of `~/.tauri/shotcap.key.pub` into
  `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` → `plugins.updater.pubkey`.
- Put the **contents** of `~/.tauri/shotcap.key` into the GitHub secret
  `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, and the password into
  `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`.

CI signs each updater artifact with this key (`tauri-action` reads the two env
vars) and `includeUpdaterJson: true` emits `latest.json` next to the binaries.

## 2. macOS self-signed code-signing cert (recommended, NO notarization)

> Why: macOS ties the **Screen Recording** TCC grant to the app's code
> signature. An *unsigned* (ad-hoc) app gets a new transient identity on every
> build, so the user must re-grant Screen Recording after **every** update. A
> stable self-signed identity keeps the grant. We deliberately skip Apple
> notarization (no paid Developer ID); users do a one-time right-click → Open /
> System Settings → Privacy → Screen Recording grant on first launch.

Create the cert in **Keychain Access** (one-time, on a Mac):

```
Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a Certificate…
  Name:            Shotcap Self-Signed
  Identity Type:   Self Signed Root
  Certificate Type: Code Signing
  ☑ Let me override defaults → keep defaults, finish.
```

or fully scripted:

```bash
# 1) Cert config
cat > shotcap-codesign.cnf <<'EOF'
[ req ]
distinguished_name = dn
x509_extensions = v3
prompt = no
[ dn ]
CN = Shotcap Self-Signed
[ v3 ]
basicConstraints = critical,CA:false
keyUsage = critical,digitalSignature
extendedKeyUsage = critical,codeSigning
EOF

# 2) Key + self-signed cert
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem \
  -days 3650 -nodes -config shotcap-codesign.cnf

# 3) Bundle into a .p12 (set a strong export password)
openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey key.pem -in cert.pem \
  -name "Shotcap Self-Signed" -out shotcap-codesign.p12

# 4) The signing identity string is the certificate CN:
#    APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY = "Shotcap Self-Signed"
```

Base64-encode the `.p12` for the GitHub secret:

```bash
base64 -i shotcap-codesign.p12 | pbcopy   # → paste into APPLE_CERTIFICATE
```

First-launch on the user's Mac: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen
Recording → enable Shotcap, then quit & reopen (TCC requires a restart). Because
the identity is stable, this is needed once, not per update.

## 3. Windows / Linux (optional placeholders)

The workflow has `Sign Windows installers (placeholder)` and `Sign Linux
packages (placeholder)` steps that **skip automatically** when their secrets are
absent. To enable Windows Authenticode later, prefer wiring
`bundle.windows.signCommand` in `tauri.conf.json` so signing runs before
`latest.json` hashing.

---

## 4. Complete GitHub secrets list

| Secret | Required | Used by | Notes |
|--------|----------|---------|-------|
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | **Yes** | updater signing (all platforms) | contents of `~/.tauri/shotcap.key` |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | **Yes** | updater signing | password set during `tauri signer generate` |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` | mac only | keychain import | base64 of the `.p12` |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | mac only | keychain import | `.p12` export password |
| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | mac only | `codesign` identity selection | the cert CN, e.g. `Shotcap Self-Signed` |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` | optional | signtool placeholder | base64 of `.pfx` |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | optional | signtool placeholder | |
| `LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` | optional | gpg placeholder | armored private key |
| `LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE` | optional | gpg placeholder | |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | auto | release upload | provided by Actions |

## 5. Cutting a release

```bash
# bump apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json + package.json version, commit, then:
git tag desktop-v0.1.0
git push origin desktop-v0.1.0
```

This runs `desktop-release.yml`, produces signed installers + `latest.json`,
and opens a **draft** GitHub release. Review the assets, then publish. The
`latest` release's `latest.json` is what the updater endpoint resolves to.

steps: Add the new workflow file at the REPO ROOT as .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml (GitHub only executes workflows from the root .github/workflows/, not from apps/desktop/). Use the desktop-v* tag trigger so it never collides with the extension's existing v* build.yml. Leave the extension's build.yml untouched — both release flows coexist by tag namespace.

In tauri-action's `with:` block set `projectPath: apps/desktop` so it locates package.json + src-tauri under the monorepo subdir. Keep `args: ${{ matrix.args }}` exactly as curvault for the mac universal target.

Generate the minisign updater keypair on a trusted machine: `npm --prefix apps/desktop run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/shotcap.key`. Paste the .pub contents into tauri.conf.json plugins.updater.pubkey; store the private key + password as TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY / TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD secrets.

Set tauri.conf.json: plugins.updater.active=true, dialog=false, endpoints=[https://github.com/wa-otomia/shot2issue/releases/latest/download/latest.json] (matches the extension repo, which the monorepo keeps), and bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts=true. Adjust the repo slug if the monorepo is renamed.

On a Mac, create a self-signed Code Signing certificate (Keychain Access Certificate Assistant, or the scripted openssl path in SIGNING.md). Export to .p12, base64-encode it into APPLE_CERTIFICATE, set APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD and APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY (= the cert CN) as secrets.

Add the GitHub secrets listed in SIGNING.md section 4. The macOS keychain-import step and both OS-signing placeholders are guarded by `env.X != ''`, so forks/PRs and runs without the optional secrets skip them cleanly.

Wire the updater UI in the desktop app the same way curvault does: a thin src/lib/api.ts wrapper over the plugin's check()/downloadAndInstall(), plus the lightweight GitHub-releases-API notifier if a 'check now' affordance is wanted (copy curvault's services/updates.rs verbatim, swapping the repo slug).

Cut a release: bump version in apps/desktop/{package.json,src-tauri/tauri.conf.json}, commit, `git tag desktop-v0.1.0 && git push origin desktop-v0.1.0`. Review the draft release, confirm latest.json + signed installers are attached, then publish.
risks: GitHub Actions ONLY runs workflows located at <repo-root>/.github/workflows/. A file physically under apps/desktop/.github/workflows/ will NOT trigger. The workflow must live at repo root; `projectPath: apps/desktop` is what scopes it to the subdir. The file list above flags this explicitly.

Order-of-operations for OS signing vs latest.json: tauri-action generates latest.json (and the .sig minisign signatures) DURING the bundle step. The Windows/Linux placeholder steps run AFTER, so any binary they sign is NOT the one referenced by latest.json hashes. For production Windows signing, use bundle.windows.signCommand in tauri.conf.json (signs before hashing) rather than the post-build placeholder. The minisign update signature is unaffected — it is what the updater actually verifies.

macOS self-signed (non-notarized) apps trip Gatekeeper on first launch: users must right-click → Open, or approve under System Settings → Privacy & Security. The Screen Recording grant additionally needs an app restart. Document this clearly to users; it is inherent to skipping notarization, not a bug.

The TCC-grant-survives-update behavior depends on the code signature being byte-stable across builds (same cert, same identity). If the .p12/cert is ever regenerated, existing users will have to re-grant Screen Recording. Treat the cert as long-lived (10y validity in the doc) and back it up securely.

tauri-action's macOS signing path expects APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY to match an identity present in the keychain search list. The import step sets the keychain search list, but if the runner's login keychain ordering differs across runner image versions, `codesign` may not find the key. Verify `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` lists the identity (the step prints it).

Universal mac build requires both aarch64 and x86_64 Rust targets; the matrix conditional installs them. If the desktop app pulls a crate without an x86_64-apple-darwin prebuilt (e.g. a native dep), the universal build can fail where a single-arch build would pass — verify on real mac.

Wayland: global-shortcut + live overlay are unsupported (given constraint). This does not affect the release/signing flow, but the Linux .deb/.AppImage will ship a degraded capture path; CI cannot detect this. Out of scope for this subsystem but worth noting in release notes.

Secret name collision: the extension's build.yml uses GITHUB_TOKEN only. The new desktop secrets (TAURI_*, APPLE_*) are additive and unused by build.yml, so no collision. Confirm no org-level secret naming policy blocks them.

criticalRisks: App-identity conflict across subsystems: tauri-shell + capture use productName 'shot2issue' / com.waotomia.shot2issue, while editor-reuse + ci-signing use 'Shotcap' / com.waotomia.shotcap with desktop-v* tags. These MUST be unified to ONE name+identifier+repo-slug+tag-namespace before Phase 3 or the updater pubkey/endpoint, bundle identifier, and TCC grant will not match. Pick once and propagate.

Workflows must live at <repo-root>/.github/workflows/. .github/ stays at root after the move; both build.yml (v*) and desktop-release.yml (desktop-v*) live there. A naive `git mv .github apps/extension/` silently disables ALL CI. Also: build.yml's paths: filter applies to tag pushes too — real extension releases bump apps/extension/{package.json,src/manifest.json} so the filter matches, but a tag touching only outside apps/extension/** would be skipped.

macOS Screen Recording (TCC) is the crux of the self-signing decision and is UNPROVEN by curvault (which has no screen capture). xcap returns black frames until the user grants Screen Recording + restarts; the grant is anchored to a STABLE code signature. The whole self-signed-in-CI design rests on the assumption that a stable .p12 identity keeps the grant across auto-updates — must be validated end-to-end on a real Mac (grant on vN, auto-update to vN+1, confirm capture still returns real pixels without re-prompting). Regenerating the cert revokes all users' grants.

WKWebView enforces CORS strictly, so ALL provider/AI network IO MUST go through tauri-plugin-http (Rust reqwest); any ported code still calling window.fetch silently fails on macOS. The CSP connect-src is locked to self+ipc deliberately. The http:default capability host allowlist must stay in sync with the providers' real endpoints (self-hosted GitLab/YouTrack use arbitrary hosts — the wildcard allows are broad).

GitHub provider is a true rewrite, not a port — the highest-uncertainty piece. The extension uses NO token (chrome.scripting injection into github.com's same-origin composer); Tauri has no analogue. The PAT path has no first-class issue-attachment API: Contents-API/gist uploads work, but private-repo raw image URLs require auth to render and may 404 for other viewers. Codex OAuth redirect is host-exact: apps/extension/src/lib/ai.ts:5 states only http://localhost:1455 is registered and chromiumapp.org is rejected. The loopback design uses 127.0.0.1:1455 — if the OAuth client requires the literal 'localhost', the Rust server must bind/advertise 'localhost' and exchangeCode must send the identical redirect_uri, or token exchange fails.

Coordinate-space correctness across mixed-DPI multi-monitor is the biggest capture bug surface: xcap reports/captures in DEVICE px, the overlay window is sized in LOGICAL px, and tauri cursor_position's logical/physical-ness varies by platform. The design funnels everything through one per-monitor scale and reports logical px, but the exact behavior must be verified per-OS (Retina+external on mac, Windows scaling).

Native Wayland breaks both the global hotkey (stock plugin can't grab) and the transparent always-on-top overlay (tao can't position/raise). The degrade path (capture full screen → crop in a normal window + tray-menu trigger) is designed but must actually be wired in HomeView/Overlay/tray, or Linux/Wayland users get a non-functional app.

Order-of-operations: OS code-signing vs latest.json. tauri-action generates latest.json + minisign .sig DURING bundling; the Win/Linux signing placeholders run AFTER, so any binary they sign is NOT the one latest.json hashes. Production Windows signing must move to tauri.conf.json bundle.windows.signCommand (signs before hashing). The minisign update signature — what the updater actually verifies — is unaffected.

Streaming + multipart through tauri-plugin-http are unverified on a real WebView: the AI title/thinking stream needs incremental chunks via res.body.getReader() (if reqwest buffers, the live stream degrades to one late update), and GitLab/YouTrack FormData multipart must preserve the boundary through Rust reqwest.
